column1: # The procfs mount scenario, driven by `just test-procfs <arch>`.
# `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` item 7 wired the procfs server: a boot process of its own
# (`/sbin/procfs`, endpoint 21), an initramfs entry, and a mount at `/proc` in VFS.
# Nothing else in the tree opens a path under a user-mounted VTreeFS, so the
# server's own unit tests drive `handle_fs_message` directly and never involve VFS
# or MFS. This step is what proves the mount crossed the boundary: VFS resolves
# `/proc` in MFS, records the vmnt, and asks procfs for the rest of the path.
# The client's fields are separate claims, so a mount that half-works cannot read as
# a pass. `hz` is `/proc/hz`, a positive decimal from the kernel clock (`SYS_TIMES`).
# `uptime` is `/proc/uptime`, `<seconds>.<hundredths>`, which is C's `%ld.%02ld`
# `load` is `/proc/loadavg`, three `%ld.%02ld` figures the kernel's
# `GET_LOADINFO` supplies. `dir` is `/proc` itself resolving to a directory through the
# root listing, read with `getdents` the way `ls` reads it: `hz`,
# `uptime`, `loadavg` and one directory per live process, each exactly once. That is
# the claim a listing bug broke (every PID directory was invisible and the first static
# file repeated once per process slot). `self` is `/proc/self`, a link whose target is
# the asking process's own `/proc/<pid>`: its target depends on the caller, so it only
# reads back if VFS passed the caller's endpoint through the mount. `exe` is
# caller's endpoint through the mount. `exe` is
# `/proc/self/exe` read through that link, which is `/bin/procfsprobe`. `name` is
# `/proc/self/status`, whose `Name:` field has to be the program the probe was exec'd
# from, which PM records at `execve`. `gone` is a
# path under `/proc` that is not there: it has to be the mounted tree's own `ENOENT`
# (2), which is only reachable if VFS split the path at `/proc` rather than falling
# through to the root filesystem.
# The same line holds on all three arches because none of the claims is a number the
# arch chooses: the files are parsed, not compared, the listing is checked for shape
# rather than contents, and the refusals are errnos.
/bin/procfsprobe
column2: procfs: hz=ok uptime=ok load=ok dir=ok list=ok self=ok exe=ok name=ok gone=err 2
